title: Protective effect of olopatadine hydrochloride against LPS-induced acute lung injury: via targeting NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Kaur, Jaspreet; Rana, Priyanka; Matta, Tushar; Sodhi, Rupinder Kaur; Pathania, Khushboo; Pawar, Sandip V; Kuhad, Anurag; Kondepudi, Kanthi Kiran; Kaur, Tanzeer; Dhingra, Neelima; Sah, Sangeeta Pilkhwal
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子对接筛选NF-kappaB抑制剂并验证其抗炎作用，虽涉及转录因子但核心是药物药效与疾病模型，缺乏蛋白-DNA互作机制与AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Morbidity and mortality rates associated with acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome (ALI/ARDS) are high (30-40%). Nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-kappaB) is a transcription factor, associated with transcription of numerous cytokines leading to cytokine storm, and thereby, plays a major role in ALI/ARDS and in advanced COVID-19 syndrome. METHODS: Considering the role of NF-kappaB in ALI, cost-effective in silico approaches were utilized in the study to identify potential NF-kappaB inhibitor based on the docking and pharmacokinetic results. The identified compound was then pharmacologically validated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS) rodent model of acute lung injury. LPS induces ALI by altering alveolar membrane permeability, recruiting activated neutrophils and macrophages to the lungs, and compromising the alveolar membrane integrity and ultimately impairs the gaseous exchange. Furthermore, LPS exposure is associated with exaggerated production of various proinflammatory cytokines in lungs. RESULTS: Based on in silico studies Olopatadine Hydrochloride (Olo), an FDA-approved drug was found as a potential NF-kappaB inhibitor which has been reported for the first time, and considered further for the pharmacological validation. Intraperitoneal LPS administration resulted in ALI/ARDS by fulfilling 3 out of the 4 criteria described by ATS committee (2011) published workshop report. However, treatment with Olo attenuated LPS-induced elevation of proinflammatory markers (IL-6 and NF-kappaB), oxidative stress, neutrophil infiltration, edema, and damage in lungs. Histopathological studies also revealed that Olo treatment significantly ameliorated LPS-induced lung injury, thus conferring improvement in survival. Especially, the effects produced by Olo medium dose (1 mg/kg) were comparable to dexamethasone standard. CONCLUSION: In nutshell, inhibition of NF-kappaB pathway by Olo resulted in protection and reduced mortality in LPS- induced ALI and thus has potential to be used clinically to arrest disease progression in ALI/ARDS, since the drug is already in the market. However, the findings warrant further extensive studies, and also future studies can be planned to elucidate its role in COVID-19-associated ARDS or cytokine storm.
abstract_zh: 背景：急性肺损伤/急性呼吸窘迫综合征（ALI/ARDS）相关的发病率和死亡率较高（30-40%）。核因子-κB（NF-kappaB）是一种转录因子，与多种细胞因子的转录相关，导致细胞因子风暴，从而在ALI/ARDS及晚期COVID-19综合征中发挥重要作用。方法：鉴于NF-kappaB在ALI中的作用，本研究采用成本效益高的计算机模拟方法，基于对接和药代动力学结果识别潜在的NF-kappaB抑制剂。随后，在脂多糖（LPS）诱导的急性肺损伤啮齿动物模型中对该化合物进行了药理学验证。LPS通过改变肺泡膜通透性、招募活化中性粒细胞和巨噬细胞至肺部、损害肺泡膜完整性并最终影响气体交换来诱导ALI。此外，LPS暴露与肺部多种促炎细胞因子的过度产生相关。结果：基于计算机模拟研究，奥洛他定盐酸盐（Olo），一种FDA批准的药物，被发现为潜在的NF-kappaB抑制剂，这是首次报道，并进一步考虑进行药理学验证。腹腔注射LPS通过满足ATS委员会（2011年）发布的研讨会报告中4项标准中的3项，诱导了ALI/ARDS。然而，Olo治疗减弱了LPS诱导的促炎标志物（IL-6和NF-kappaB）升高、氧化应激、中性粒细胞浸润、水肿及肺部损伤。组织病理学研究也显示，Olo治疗显著改善了LPS诱导的肺损伤，从而提高了生存率。特别是，Olo中剂量（1 mg/kg）产生的效果与地塞米松标准相当。结论：总之，Olo通过抑制NF-kappaB通路在LPS诱导的ALI中提供了保护并降低了死亡率，因此，由于该药物已在市场上销售，具有临床用于阻止ALI/ARDS疾病进展的潜力。然而，这些发现需要进一步广泛研究，未来研究也可计划阐明其在COVID-19相关ARDS或细胞因子风暴中的作用。
